hints: Use an array as a stack of opening brackets.

`if let open = pairs[ch] { guard stack.popLast() == open else { return false } } else { stack.append(ch) }`.
jsBridge: The classic stack problem. In Swift, `[Character]` works as the stack (`append`/`popLast`), and a `[Character: Character]` map pairs brackets. `popLast()` returns an optional where JS `pop()` returns `undefined`.

compass.q: JS `pop()` on an empty array returns `undefined`. Swift `popLast()` returns `nil` while `removeLast()` crashes. Which do you want here?
